description: Backend Part C (collector business accounts + S3-backed verification) and Part D (admins group check + verification queue), plus the prefix-based dispatcher that routes /collector/ and /admin/ in front of the existing endswith chain. Depends on FEAT-002 (the collector scaffolding _get_collector/_is_approved_collector/DOC_TYPES/s3 client already exist) and FEAT-001 (the env vars/table/bucket exist at deploy time). Includes NIT#5 (upload contentType allow-list) and NIT#7 (token-scoped admin comment).
steps: In lambdas/collect/app.py add the collector route handlers: POST /collector/apply (upsert a 'draft' record with status 'draft', createdAt, updatedAt — idempotent, re-apply keeps data); POST /collector/submit ('draft'->'pending', validate non-empty required fields in order businessName, registrationNumber, wasteCarrierLicense, serviceAreas (non-empty list), wasteCategories (non-empty list), contactPhone, contactEmail -> 400 naming the first missing; reject if already approved/pending -> 409; set updatedAt; notify applicant); GET /collector/me (the caller's record or {'status':'none'}). All timestamps epoch seconds via int(time.time()).

Add POST /collector/upload-url: body {docType, contentType}; validate docType in DOC_TYPES -> 400; NIT#5: validate contentType against the allow-list {'image/png','image/jpeg','application/pdf'} -> 400 otherwise; key is 'collectors/{userId}/{docType}'; return {url, key} from s3.generate_presigned_url('put_object', Params={Bucket, Key, ContentType}, ExpiresIn=300) (the signed ContentType MUST equal the browser PUT Content-Type); record the key in docKeys[docType] on the collector record.

Add _is_admin(claims): return 'admins' in (claims.get('cognito:groups') or []). NIT#7: add a one-line comment near the check that cognito:groups is token-scoped, so a newly-added admin must re-login / wait for token refresh before admin routes work.

Add the admin routes: GET /admin/collectors?status=pending (_is_admin gate 403; validate status against {pending,approved,rejected,suspended}, default pending, else 400; query collectors.statusIndex newest-first; for each docKeys entry attach a presigned GET URL ExpiresIn=300, tolerating a missing object); POST /admin/collectors/{id}/approve ('pending'->'approved', set verifiedAt=int(time.time()), verifiedBy=sub, updatedAt; notify; 409 if not pending, 404 if missing); POST /admin/collectors/{id}/reject (body {reason}, 'pending'->'rejected', store rejectionReason=_s(...)[:1000], notify with reason, 409/404 as above); POST /admin/collectors/{id}/suspend ('approved'->'suspended', notify, 409 if not approved). {id} is the collector userId.

Add the prefix-based dispatcher to handler(): in the POST branch, BEFORE the existing endswith chain, add 'if route.startswith("/admin/"): return _unwrap(dispatch_admin(claims, route, body))' and 'if route.startswith("/collector/"): return _unwrap(dispatch_collector(claims, route, body))'. Also add new endswith suffixes to the chain: 'confirm' -> confirm_deal, 'cancel' -> cancel_request, 'dispute' -> raise_dispute (keep report/request/approve/reject/done/message/subscribe/unsubscribe/read). In the GET branch, BEFORE the existing suffix chain, add 'if route.startswith("/collector/"): return _unwrap(dispatch_collector_get(claims, route))' and 'if route.startswith("/admin/"): return _unwrap(dispatch_admin_get(claims, route))'.

Implement dispatch_admin(claims, route, body): split route on '/' into ['','admin','collectors','<id>','<action>'], validate action in {approve,reject,suspend} -> 400, check _is_admin FIRST -> 403, call the matching function with the parsed id. Implement dispatch_collector (apply/submit/upload-url), dispatch_collector_get (/collector/me), dispatch_admin_get (GET /admin/collectors). RATIONALE: a naive /admin/collectors/{id}/approve is otherwise captured by route.endswith('approve') -> approve_request (verified real collision), hence prefix-first.
acceptance_criteria: lambdas/collect/app.py still imports cleanly under the stubs; pytest collection succeeds.
The four collector routes (apply/submit/me/upload-url) and four admin routes (list/approve/reject/suspend) exist with the specified status transitions and error codes.
upload-url rejects a docType outside DOC_TYPES and a contentType outside {image/png,image/jpeg,application/pdf} with 400; presigns with ExpiresIn=300 and the browser's ContentType.
_is_admin reads only claims['cognito:groups'] and carries the token-scoped comment; every admin route checks _is_admin first (403).
The prefix dispatcher routes /admin/ and /collector/ before the endswith chain so /admin/collectors/{id}/approve is NOT captured by endswith('approve'); confirm/cancel/dispute suffixes are wired.
verification: From the worktree root run 'pytest -q' and confirm all existing unit tests still pass (import + _is_admin behavior; FEAT-004 adds the _is_admin assertions).
Re-read handler() and confirm the two POST prefix checks and two GET prefix checks precede the endswith chain, and that confirm/cancel/dispute suffixes are present.

Trace dispatch_admin on the literal route '/admin/collectors/abc123/approve' and confirm it parses id='abc123', action='approve', checks _is_admin, and calls the approve function (not approve_request).
findings:
Implemented in lambdas/collect/app.py. All 30 existing tests pass (pytest -q). Routes for the frontend (collectFetch bearer helper; all take Authorization: Bearer <idToken>):

COLLECTOR (self-service, any logged-in user):
- POST /collector/apply  body {businessName, registrationNumber, wasteCarrierLicense, serviceAreas:[], wasteCategories:[], contactPhone, contactEmail} -> idempotent upsert of a 'draft' record (re-apply keeps data, never regresses pending/approved). Returns _collector_view.
- POST /collector/submit  (no body needed) -> 'draft'->'pending'; validates required fields in this order: businessName, registrationNumber, wasteCarrierLicense, contactPhone, contactEmail, then serviceAreas (non-empty list), then wasteCategories (non-empty list); 400 names the first missing field; 409 if already pending/approved; 404 if never applied. Notifies applicant (push type 'request').
- GET  /collector/me  -> the caller's record or {'status':'none'}. _collector_view shape: {status, businessName, registrationNumber, wasteCarrierLicense, serviceAreas, wasteCategories, contactPhone, contactEmail, docKeys, rejectionReason, createdAt, updatedAt, verifiedAt}.
- POST /collector/upload-url  body {docType, contentType} -> {url, key}. docType must be in DOC_TYPES {registration, license, insurance} else 400; contentType must be in UPLOAD_CONTENT_TYPES {image/png, image/jpeg, application/pdf} (NIT#5) else 400. Returns a presigned PUT (ExpiresIn=300). FRONTEND MUST send the PUT with the exact same Content-Type header as the contentType it requested (the signed ContentType must match the browser PUT Content-Type) or S3 rejects it. Key is collectors/{userId}/{docType}; recorded in docKeys[docType] on the record.

ADMIN (requires 'admins' Cognito group; _is_admin checks claims['cognito:groups'] only). NIT#7: cognito:groups is TOKEN-SCOPED — a user newly added to the admins group must re-login / wait for ID-token refresh before admin routes work. Every admin route returns 403 if not admin.
- GET  /admin/collectors?status=pending  -> {collectors:[...]}. status in {pending,approved,rejected,suspended} (default pending; 400 otherwise). Newest-first via collectors statusIndex. Each item = _collector_view + userId + docUrls (map docType->presigned GET URL, ExpiresIn=300; missing/unpresignable docs are skipped, not fatal).
- POST /admin/collectors/{id}/approve  -> 'pending'->'approved' (sets verifiedAt, verifiedBy, updatedAt); 409 if not pending; 404 if missing; notifies (push type 'approved'). {id} is the collector userId.
- POST /admin/collectors/{id}/reject   body {reason} -> 'pending'->'rejected' (stores rejectionReason[:1000]); 409/404 as above; notifies with reason (push type 'rejected').
- POST /admin/collectors/{id}/suspend  -> 'approved'->'suspended'; 409 if not approved; notifies (push type 'rejected').

DISPATCHER (handler() in lambdas/collect/app.py): PREFIX dispatch added IN FRONT of the endswith chain. POST: route.startswith('/admin/')->dispatch_admin, route.startswith('/collector/')->dispatch_collector, both before any endswith. GET: route.startswith('/collector/')->dispatch_collector_get then route.startswith('/admin/')->dispatch_admin_get, before the endswith chain. dispatch_admin splits the path into ['','admin','collectors','<id>','<action>'], validates action in {approve,reject,suspend} (400 else), checks _is_admin FIRST (403), then calls the matching admin_* function with the parsed id. This is REQUIRED because /admin/collectors/{id}/approve would otherwise be captured by route.endswith('approve')->approve_request (verified: traced '/admin/collectors/abc123/approve' -> id='abc123', action='approve', reaches admin_approve_collector, NOT approve_request). Also wired the FEAT-002 state-machine suffixes into the POST endswith chain: 'confirm'->confirm_deal, 'cancel'->cancel_request, 'dispute'->raise_dispute (each posts {collectRequestId}; dispute also reads {reason}).

VERIFIED: pytest -q = 30 passed; dispatch_admin trace confirmed id/action parse + _is_admin-first gate; _is_admin({})==False and _is_admin({'cognito:groups':['admins']})==True; prefix checks precede endswith chains in both POST and GET. No new real-payment code added (FEAT-003 adds none). FRONTEND (Part E / FEAT): add a Profile collector-account section calling apply/submit/upload-url/me, and an admin overlay calling the four /admin routes; Auth.profile() must expose a 'groups' field so the SPA can show/hide the admin overlay (the backend still re-checks _is_admin on every admin call).
